correctness.rationale: For G=K_N minus an edge-disjoint star forest (M≤N−2), G is connected of diameter ≤2 and its anchored dual Lipschitz ball has the stated unit edge-difference constraints. The equilateral baseline coordinate volume is N. For one removed star with m leaves, fix center to 0 and condition on k=N−m−1 remaining clique coordinates of range r≤1 in [−1,1]; the leaf conditional volume in an interval length 2−r with mutual range≤1 equals m+1−mr. Integrating standard range densities yields V=N+2m/(N−m), including k=1. For several disjoint missing stars, any extra point beyond the equilateral ball has a min/max pair at a nonedge within a unique star, with all vertices outside this component in an interval of length <1; exceptional regions from different stars have disjoint interiors, and other-star constraints become automatic. Thus volumes add N+Σ2m_i/(N−m_i). At fixed total M, φ(m)=2m/(N−m) strictly superadditive under merging (one star uniquely maximal) and has increasing finite differences (balanced, maximally numerous disjoint stars uniquely minimal). Independently enumerated exact Ehrhart leading coefficients for N=4,5 with group patterns [1], [1,1], [2] match 14/3,6,19/3; the analytic proof covers all N, M.
